answer: Stake-weighted identity in an agent economy makes a sybil attack expensive: each agent must bond collateral tied to a verified operator, and peers only count attestations from seats that have built a track record. A forge of fake identities then costs real capital per seat. Crystal clear accounting of bonds and slashing makes the cost visible to everyone, while dune-style sampling of random graders keeps any single cluster of colluding agents from controlling the verdict.
